newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma bomb defense wants trial moved.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma bomb defense wants trial moved.

text.p: The second Oklahoma City bombing trial should not be held in Denver because potential jurors in Colorado are too emotionally involved with the blast victims, defendant Terry Nichols' lawyers argued.
Instead, they said in a court filing made public on Tuesday that the trial should be moved to San Francisco.
They also said there was no need to delay the Sept. 29 scheduled start of the trial.

"(Prospective) jurors feel a personal stake in the outcome" of Nichols' trial because news coverage in Colorado of co-defendant Timothy McVeigh's recent trial focused heavily on emotional aspects of the bombing, the lawyers contended.
In June McVeigh was found guilty and sentenced to death for the April 19, 1995 bombing of Oklahoma City's Alfred P. Murrah federal building that killed 168 people.
Nichols is accused of conspiring with and helping his former army buddy.
Prosecutors in their strongly worded court filing accused the defence of "forum shopping" and said the trial would have to be delayed if it were moved.

"The court should deny this transparant attempt to forum shop. (San Francisco's) reputation as a liberal, anti-death penalty jurisdiction is well known," prosecutors said. They also said Nichols can receive a fair trial in Denver.
Nichols' lawyers said news coverage in San Francisco of McVeigh's trial was "at a constant and low level" compared with intense coverage in Colorado.

Coloradoans offered so much sympathy and support for survivors of the bombing and relatives of those killed that "by the time the McVeigh trial was over, Denver had become a 'sister city' to Oklahoma City," Nichols' lawyers claimed.
The same circumstances that caused U.S. District Judge Richard Matsch to move the trial from Oklahoma to Denver now exist in Colorado, Nichols' lawyers argued.
Matsch will also make the decision on the defence request to move the trial again.

On Wednesday, Matsch is to hear arguments on a defence request to bar the U.S. attorney in Oklahoma City, Pat Ryan, from Nichols' trial. Nichols' lawyers claim Ryan is so emotionally involved that he may unfairly influence jurors.
